name: MathVista
description: MathVista is a benchmark designed to evaluate mathematical reasoning of foundation models in visual contexts. It consists of 6,141 examples derived from 28 existing multimodal datasets involving mathematics and 3 newly created datasets (IQTest, FunctionQA, and PaperQA). The benchmark covers seven mathematical reasoning types (algebraic, arithmetic, geometry, logical, numeric common sense, scientific, and statistical reasoning) and five primary tasks (figure question answering, geometry problem solving, math word problem, textbook question answering, and visual question answering) across diverse visual contexts.
creator: Pan Lu, Hritik Bansal, Tony Xia, Jiacheng Liu, Chunyuan Li, Hannaneh Hajishirzi, Hao Cheng, Kai-Wei Chang, Michel Galley, Jianfeng Gao
citeAs: Lu et al., MathVista: Evaluating Mathematical Reasoning of Foundation Models in Visual Contexts, ICLR 2024. arXiv:2310.02255
rai:dataCollection: MathVista was collected by: (1) collecting nine MathQA datasets in multimodal settings; (2) reviewing more than 70 VQA datasets and collecting 19 that contain math-related instances; (3) creating three new datasets (IQTest, FunctionQA, PaperQA) to address gaps in logical reasoning on puzzle test diagrams, statistical reasoning on functional plots, and scientific reasoning on academic figures. Each source dataset is limited to up to 400 examples to ensure balanced representation.
rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Manual Human Curator, Web Scraping
rai:dataCollectionMissingData: Only 85.6% of examples have annotations (5,261 out of 6,141). Annotations were sourced from original data providers, and due to the heterogeneity of these sources, not all examples have annotations and they lack a unified format and structure.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Data was sourced from 28 existing multimodal datasets (9 MathQA datasets and 19 VQA datasets) and 3 newly created datasets. IQTest examples were sourced from puzzle test figures on online learning platforms. FunctionQA examples were created from functional plots. PaperQA examples were sourced from papers released in August 2023 on Huggingface (https://huggingface.co/papers).
rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: PaperQA sourced from papers released in August 2023. Multimodal Bard evaluation dates range from Sep 8, 2023 to Sep 10, 2023. GPT-4V evaluation dates range from Oct 7, 2023 to Oct 15, 2023.
rai:dataManipulationProtocol: For VQA datasets, heuristic rules were designed to automatically select examples likely to involve mathematical reasoning: examples with numeric answers or those containing quantity words in the questions were selected. This automatic filtration yielded 4,949 VQA-format examples. Each source dataset was limited to up to 400 examples to ensure balanced representation. The dataset was divided into testmini (1,000 examples) and test (5,141 examples) subsets using a sampling strategy to ensure each source dataset is well represented.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: For VQA datasets, heuristic rules were used to automatically select math-related examples (numeric answers or quantity words). Three expert annotators then manually labeled these examples to determine if they involve mathematical reasoning, using majority voting. For the three new datasets, all questions were manually annotated by graduate students in STEM fields and refined through a rigorous review process. Coarse labels of mathematical reasoning were automatically obtained from source dataset details, and verified by expert annotators for 1,000 examples.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: For VQA datasets: three expert annotators manually labeled examples to determine if they involve mathematical reasoning, using majority voting. For the three new datasets (IQTest, FunctionQA, PaperQA): questions were manually annotated by graduate students in STEM fields. A two-step process was used: each dataset was independently annotated by three reviewers, achieving 99.2% inter-annotation consistency rate. Among 736 newly collected questions, only 6 exhibited disagreements, which were resolved through discussion among the entire review team. For mathematical reasoning category labeling: expert annotators manually labeled 1,000 examples from seven reasoning type candidates. Human performance baseline was established using Amazon Mechanical Turk (AMT) with annotators required to have a high school diploma or higher, a history of more than 5,000 HIT tasks, and an acceptance score higher than 0.99.
rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: Custom annotation tool (GUI shown in Figure 23 for new datasets, Figure 22 for mathematical reasoning labeling, Figure 24 for mathematical reasoning skills labeling). Amazon Mechanical Turk (AMT) for human performance baseline and Multimodal Bard assessment task.
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Inter-annotator agreement for VQA mathematical reasoning labeling was measured using Fleiss Kappa score of 0.775, indicating substantial consistency. For the three new datasets, inter-annotation consistency rate was 99.2% (only 6 out of 736 questions had disagreements). For automatic mathematical reasoning category annotation, 94.1% of examples had exact same set of reasoning types between automatic and human annotations, and 98.79% of individual labels were identical.
rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The answer labels for the test set will not be publicly released to prevent data contamination; an online evaluation platform will be maintained. The benchmark is part of an ongoing research process with commitment to maintaining the datasets (refining potential data noise in response to community feedback) and evolving the leaderboard in response to new models.
rai:personalSensitiveInformation: Human performance annotators provided information regarding their highest level of educational attainment. Only results from annotators with a high school diploma or higher were retained.
rai:dataSocialImpact: MathVista aims to facilitate the development of AI agents capable of tackling mathematically intensive and visually rich real-world tasks, with applications in educational disciplines, logical queries about statistical data, theorem proving, and scientific discovery. The benchmark highlights a significant gap between current AI models and human performance, underscoring the need for improvements in mathematical reasoning with visual understanding.
rai:dataBiases: The dataset's focus on mathematical reasoning within visual contexts spanning specific domains like science and college-level math may limit generalizability to other domains. The dataset contains 6.57% non-English questions (Chinese and Persian), which may affect model performance on multilingual tasks. The grade level distribution (elementary, high school, college) may introduce biases in model evaluation.
rai:dataLimitations: While MathVista encompasses a broad spectrum of tasks and visual contexts, there may be gaps in the representation of certain types of mathematical problems and visuals. The scalability and generalizability of the benchmark to other domains remain a concern. Annotations lack a unified format and structure due to heterogeneity of sources. Only 85.6% of examples have annotations. The benchmark focused exclusively on the most recent and prominent models at the time of study.
rai:dataUseCases: MathVista is designed for evaluating (testing/benchmarking) mathematical reasoning capabilities of foundation models (LLMs and LMMs) in visual contexts. The testmini subset (1,000 examples) is intended for model development validation or for those with limited computing resources. The test set (5,141 examples) is for standard evaluation. The benchmark supports fine-grained evaluation across mathematical reasoning types, visual context types, task categories, and grade levels.
rai:annotationsPerItem: For human performance baseline: 5 annotators per question. For VQA mathematical reasoning labeling and new dataset annotation: 3 annotators per example.
rai:annotatorDemographics: Human performance annotators: required to have a high school diploma or higher, history of completing more than 5,000 HIT tasks, and acceptance score higher than 0.99. New dataset annotators: graduate students in STEM fields. VQA mathematical reasoning labelers: expert annotators.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: GPT-4 (used as answer extractor with >99.5% accuracy on 200 examples). EasyOCR (JaidedAI, 2020) for OCR text detection. Multimodal Bard for image caption generation.
